title: Global optimization advances in mixed-integer nonlinear programming, MINLP, and constrained derivative-free optimization, CDFO
contribution: A joint review that maps deterministic global MINLP as one framework of competing components (reformulation, underestimators, cuts, branching, FBBT/OBBT, heuristics) and CDFO as local/global, direct/model-based and deterministic/stochastic methods; it adds a 2571-problem MINLP test suite and a size-filtered CDFO suite, and sets out an agenda for hybrid MINLP/CDFO solvers.
problem_entry: Two literatures that seem to serve different applications are shown to feed each other (decomposition, shared penalty/filter devices, surrogate fitting as global optimisation), entered through an explicit applications lens (pp. 2-3, 9).
key_idea: Global MINLP is tractable only as heterogeneous components pieced into one framework; the review advocates an 'all-of-the-above' design with relaxations competing per node, and places ANTIGONE (polymorphic term classes) and GloMIQO (structure-exploiting reformulation) in that map (pp. 2, 5, 11-13, 27).
assumptions: MINLP with finite inferable variable bounds and finite function images (p. 4), nested subclasses MIQCQP/MIQP/BQP/QAP/MISO (pp. 5-6); CDFO with known and unknown constraints and no assumptions on the black-box forms (p. 8); local DFO convergence needs smoothness (p. 17); discrete local DFO needs a user-defined neighbourhood (p. 19).
proof_devices: Horst-Tuy sufficient convergence conditions for spatial B&B (refinability, convergence of the relaxation under refinement), stated not proved (p. 13)
convex hull as the tightest convex underestimator; term-wise hulls are not the hull of the whole MINLP, so multi-term relaxations are needed (p. 14)
cluster problem and relaxation convergence rate (p. 16)

DFO geometry measures (cosine measure, simplex volume, poisedness) and stationarity as step/mesh size goes to zero (p. 17); asymptotic convergence of global surrogate methods in the limit of infinite samples (p. 21)
experiments: No new computations; assembles a 2571-problem MINLP suite with per-class provenance (Table 13, pp. 60-61; results referred to ANTIGONE paper, p. 28) and a CDFO suite filtered to at most 300 variables or constraints (Table 14, pp. 28, 62).
positioning: Augments Bussieck-Vigerske 2010, Belotti et al. 2013b and D'Ambrosio-Lodi 2013 rather than replacing them (pp. 26-27); limits its application table to nonconvex problems solved globally, unlike Belotti et al. (p. 9); defers to Rios-Sahinidis 2013 for box-constrained DFO software (p. 27); gives rival codes (BARON, Couenne, SCIP, alphaSGO, LINDO) their own rows (pp. 53-55); stresses the Floudas lineage (p. 2).
writing: First-person stance sentences ('Here we advocate...', p. 11; 'In our view, it is absolutely critical...', p. 9), hedging placed only where knowledge is missing (pp. 12, 16), coded quick-access tables (pp. 31-40), numbered open questions (p. 26), and the scope advice repeated in the conclusion (p. 29).
limits_future: Limits: best automatic reformulations unknown (p. 12), heuristics inside global optimisation little studied (pp. 15-16), floating-point and tolerance-clash numerics (p. 16), no finite global guarantee for CDFO (p. 29); future: hybrid MINLP/CDFO decompositions (pp. 25-26), surrogates with error bounds for hard terms, structure detection for black boxes via ML, global optimisation of fitted surrogates (p. 26).

method_links.note: GloMIQO presented as 'a major effort to elucidate special structure via reformulations'; MIQCQP classes shown as graph patterns; structure and sparsity detection proposed for black boxes too.

Component-in-the-whole framing: stand-alone heuristics differ from heuristics that work inside a framework; term-wise tightness is not whole-problem tightness; the ideal implementation selects algorithms per problem. Stated, not tested.
2571-problem suite with per-class provenance and complete results referred to ANTIGONE; explicit size cutoff for the CDFO suite.

2016 stated agenda: globally optimise fitted surrogates and their parameter estimation with MINLP machinery; the surrogate is still an approximation of a black box, not yet the partner's trained model taken as the problem; section authorship not stated.
FBBT vs OBBT framed as two extremes (cheap/weak vs demanding/strong), but no interpolating family is proposed.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Advocates implementing many strategies and selecting per problem; hybrid tools that exploit the tightest relaxation at each node; relaxations competing in real time in ANTIGONE and BARON.
Literature organised as the parts of one branch-and-cut algorithm, with a framework figure and per-component tables plus a solver x feature table.

transferable: Survey layout: one framework figure plus one table per algorithmic component plus a solver x feature table, so that each contribution has a slot in the pipeline (pp. 12, 45-55).
Relaxation index: rows by term type, columns by relaxation strategy, with 'Only in: <solver>' footnotes recording which terms only one code supports (Tables 1, 6; pp. 30, 45-49).
Write a scope sentence that sends readers to the neighbouring method family when an explicit formulation exists (pp. 9, 29).
Benchmark assembly with per-class source references and a stated inclusion cutoff tied to current solver capability (Tables 13-14, p. 28).
End a connections section with numbered open research questions (p. 26).
Grey-box decomposition sketch: fix the black-box variables, bound the rest with a global MINLP solver, and shrink the DFO search region (pp. 25-26).
coauthors: Fani Boukouvala (first author), Christodoulos A. Floudas (corresponding author)

quotes.text: Here we advocate an all-of-the-above approach; an ideal implementation incorporates many possible effective strategies and then selects appropriate algorithms for any given problem.
Thus, it should be stressed that when a problem can be sufficiently described by a well-posed, explicit MINLP formulation, then CDFO methods are not recommended.
